title: Singapore to Fine Bus Passengers for Bad Behavior
paragraphs: Singapore has introduced new fines for bus passengers who behave badly, as part of a crackdown on "disruptive" behavior on public transport.

Under the new rules, which took effect in late September 2026, passengers who cause annoyance to others can be fined up to 500 Singapore dollars, or about $390. According to the Land Transport Authority (LTA), which oversees public transport in Singapore, this includes playing audio loudly, putting feet on seats, littering, and eating or drinking on the bus. The rules also apply at bus interchanges and terminals.

More serious offenses carry even heavier penalties. Passengers who put other people in danger, or who make any part of a bus or transport facility dirty, can be fined up to 5,000 Singapore dollars, or about $3,900.

Bus drivers, who are known as "bus captains" in Singapore, will not issue the fines themselves. However, they can advise passengers to stop their bad behavior, ask those who refuse to get off the bus, and call for help from the police in serious cases.

The new rules bring Singapore's buses into line with the rules already in place on the city's subway system. In a statement, the LTA said that public transport is a shared space, and that every passenger has a role to play in keeping it pleasant.

Singapore is not the only place cracking down on noisy passengers. Asian transport systems are generally known for being clean and orderly, and many already ban eating, drinking or playing music on board. In London, a poll for Transport for London found that about 70% of passengers considered loud music or phone calls without headphones to be disruptive. England has also recently announced fines for bus passengers who play loud music or videos.
